review_notes: Read the whole file and checked uses of eval_nestedX/eval_nestedY elsewhere (DivisibleInflection, PolynomialLocalGraph, RealCriticalPoints). Only one repeated-proof pattern found: the identical induction in eval_nestedY and eval_nestedX. The proposed reduction via rename/eval_rename and a Fin 2 function ext is untested; the exact simp closing steps are uncertain. The other simp lemmas are short and not worth refactoring.

findings.excerpt:
induction Q using MvPolynomial.induction_on with
  | C c => simp [nestedEvalHom]
  | add P Q hP hQ => simp [map_add, hP, hQ]
  | mul_X P i hP =>
      fin_cases i
      · simp [map_mul, hP]
      · simp [map_mul, hP]
findings.problem: The two theorems have character-for-character identical proofs: an MvPolynomial.induction_on with C, add and mul_X cases, and a fin_cases on the Fin 2 index. Both are the same structural induction, once for nestedY and once for nestedX. Because nestedY is defined as (renameEquiv swap).trans nestedX, the two statements are related by a variable swap. The repeated induction is therefore redundant, and any future change to the simp set or the nestedEvalHom definition has to be made twice.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one induction and derive the other statement from it. Prove eval_nestedX by the existing induction. Then obtain eval_nestedY by unfolding the definition: nestedY R Q = nestedX R (MvPolynomial.rename (Equiv.swap 0 1) Q), using MvPolynomial.renameEquiv's coercion to rename. Apply eval_nestedX with the roles of x and y exchanged: nestedEvalHom R x y (nestedX R (rename swap Q)) = eval ![y,x] (rename swap Q). Rewrite with MvPolynomial.eval_rename to get eval (![y,x] ∘ swap 0 1) Q. Close with congr plus funext and fin_cases on Fin 2, so that ![y,x] ∘ swap 0 1 = ![x,y]. Alternatively, derive eval_nestedX from eval_nestedY using the swap, which is already used that way in DivisibleInflection. The proof sketch is untested.
findings.benefit: The induction appears once, so the file is shorter and a maintainer only needs to adjust one proof. The relation between nestedX and nestedY, which is currently implicit, becomes visible in the proof. The public statements are unchanged, so the downstream uses in DivisibleInflection, PolynomialLocalGraph and RealCriticalPoints are unaffected.

evidence.excerpt: theorem eval_rename (g : τ → R) (p : MvPolynomial σ R) : eval g (rename k p) = eval (g ∘ k) p
